l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: The unit concerns Ahura Mazda, the Amesha-Spentas, holiness, sacrifice, and the Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull. The Moon waxes for fifteen days and wanes for fifteen days, and its light causes golden-hued plants to grow during spring. The Amesha-Spentas hold the Moon’s glory and pour it upon the earth made by Mazda. Sacrifices, prayers, libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words are offered to the Moon.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is hailed, and the speaker identifies as a worshipper of Mazda who obeys the laws of Ahura. The earth is described as made by Mazda.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are hailed and are said to stand up holding the Moon’s glory and pouring it upon the earth made by Mazda.

l: Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: The Moon is hailed and worshipped as holy and master of holiness. It waxes for fifteen days and wanes for fifteen days; its light causes golden-hued plants to grow in spring, and offerings are made to it.

l: the law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: Holiness is described as the best of all good and as the law of holiness. The Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull is repeatedly called holy and master of holiness.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VII. Mâh Yast.
s: Sacrifice is offered to the Moon that keeps in it the seed of the Bull, the new moons, the full moons, the Vîshaptathas, the only-created Bull, and the Bull of many species. The offerings include libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, wisdom of the tongue, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: This unit concerns Tistrya, the bright and glorious star, and his role in bringing waters, rain, fertility, health, and protection to the material world. Ahura Mazda describes Tistrya’s worship, transformations, struggle with the Daêva Apaosha, and victory that enables waters and clouds to reach the Aryan countries. The text explains that sacrifice and prayer, performed according to the law of holiness, strengthen Tistrya and bring protection from hostile hordes, plagues, and other harms.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda establishes Tistrya as a lord and overseer above the stars and creates him as worthy of sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. He assists Tistrya, offers him a sacrifice invoked by his own name, and restores to him the strength needed to overcome the Daêva Apaosha.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Spitama Zarathustra receives Ahura Mazda’s teachings about Tistrya, his worship, transformations, battle, and role in sending waters to the world. He asks what sacrifice and invocation should properly be performed in Tistrya’s honour.

l: Tistrya, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Tistrya is the bright and glorious star who brings waters, rain, fertility, health, and protection to the material world. He battles and defeats the Daêva Apaosha, makes the sea Vouru-Kasha boil, and sends vapours, clouds, rain, and waters toward the seven Karshvares.

l: Daêva Apaosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: The Daêva Apaosha meets Tistrya at the sea Vouru-Kasha in the shape of a dark horse and fights him. He defeats Tistrya in the first three-day battle, but Tistrya later overcomes him after receiving strength through sacrifice.

l: sea Vouru-Kasha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Vouru-Kasha is the powerful, large, deep sea of salt waters where Tistrya fights Apaosha and where Tistrya and Satavaêsa rise. Tistrya makes the sea boil and sends its waters, through vapours and clouds, toward the countries of the material world.

l: Aryan countries, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: The Aryan countries depend on Tistrya for fertility, rain, and flowing waters. If they perform the proper sacrifice and invocation, hostile hordes, plagues, leprosy, venomous plants, and enemy weapons will not enter them.

l: material world, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: The material world receives waters, rain, clouds, and fertility through Tistrya’s actions. Tistrya also protects it from Pairikas and other forces that seek to extinguish its life.

l: sacrifice and prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Sacrifice and prayer addressed to Tistrya by his own name give him strength and cause him to arrive at the appointed time. The proper observance includes libations, baresma, and cooking a single-coloured head of cattle, while certain people are forbidden to take part in the offerings.

l: rain, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Rain follows the vapours and clouds that move from the sea Vouru-Kasha toward the fields and the seven Karshvares. It spreads over the lands and brings healing and fertility when Tistrya has been properly worshipped.

l: standing waters, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: The waters arise from the sea Vouru-Kasha, are divided among the countries by Apãm Napât, and flow toward fields, pastures, plants, lakes, caves, and channels. Their movement depends on Tistrya’s victory and on the wind, clouds, and rain made by Mazda.

l: fertility, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Fertility comes to the Aryan countries through Tistrya’s waters and rain. The waters reach big-seeded cornfields, small-seeded pasture-fields, beautiful places, fields, pastures, and the roots of plants so that they grow powerfully.

l: battle between Tistrya and Apaosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: Tistrya and the Daêva Apaosha fight at the sea Vouru-Kasha in the forms of white and dark horses. Apaosha first overcomes Tistrya after three days and three nights, but Tistrya later defeats him by noon after receiving the strength of ten horses, camels, bulls, mountains, and rivers.

l: Tistrya's transformations, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: For ten nights Tistrya appears in the shape of a fifteen-year-old man, for the next ten nights in the shape of a golden-horned bull, and for the following ten nights as a white, beautiful horse with golden ears and a golden caparison. He goes to the sea Vouru-Kasha in the horse shape.

l: the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, VIII. Tîr Yast.
s: The law of holiness is identified with the will of the Lord and governs the sacrifices, prayers, and invocations offered to Tistrya. Tistrya’s worship must be performed according to the perfection of holiness.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: This unit is a series of sacrifices and prayers to the powerful, holy Drvâspa, who maintains the health of flocks and assists the faithful. Haoshyangha, Yima Khshaêta, Thraêtaona, Haoma, Husravah, Zarathustra, and Kavi Vîstâspa each seek boons from Drvâspa through sacrifice, offerings, and libations. Their requests concern victory over Daêvas and enemies, prosperity and relief from suffering, the advancement of the Mazdean law, and the defeat or punishment of named foes. The unit concludes by blessing Drvâspa’s sacrifice and prayer and asking for brightness, glory, health, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is invoked at the beginning as the one whose worship and laws are followed, and the unit calls the world and Drvâspa made by Mazda.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is declared afflicted, and he is said to have created Azi Dahâka against the material world to destroy the world of the good principle.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Zarathustra is described as a worshipper of Mazda and a follower of Zarathustra, and he offers Drvâspa a sacrifice in Airyana Vaêgah to obtain Hutaosa’s adherence to the law and support for the Mazdean law.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: The Daêvas are hated and opposed by Mazda-worshippers. Haoshyangha seeks power to overcome the Daêvas of Mâzana, while Kavi Vîstâspa seeks to defeat Daêva-worshippers and enemies.

l: Drvâspa, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Drvâspa is the powerful, holy maintainer made by Mazda who keeps flocks, herds, grown-up cattle, and young ones in health and assists the faithful. She grants the requested boons to those who offer sacrifices, gifts, libations, and entreaties.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Sacrifice is repeatedly offered to Drvâspa with prayer, glorification, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, libations, and rightly-spoken words.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Prayer accompanies sacrifice and glorification to Drvâspa, and the unit blesses the sacrifice and prayer of the powerful, holy Drvâspa.

l: flocks, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Drvâspa keeps the flocks in health, and Yima Khshaêta asks her to bring fatness and flocks down to the world created by Mazda.

l: Haoshyangha, the Paradhâta, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Haoshyangha, the Paradhâta, offers Drvâspa a sacrifice on the enclosure of the Hara and receives the boon of overcoming the Daêvas of Mâzana without fearing them.

l: Yima Khshaêta, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Yima Khshaêta, the good shepherd, sacrifices to Drvâspa from the height Hukairya. He asks for fatness, flocks, and immortality and for the removal of hunger, thirst, old age, death, hot wind, and cold wind from the Mazda-created world for a thousand years.

l: Thraêtaona, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Thraêtaona, heir of the valiant Âthwya clan, sacrifices to Drvâspa in the four-cornered Varena. He asks to overcome Azi Dahâka and deliver Savanghavâk and Erenavâk.

l: Drug, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Azi Dahâka is described as a three-mouthed, three-headed, six-eyed, thousand-sensed fiendish Drug created by Angra Mainyu against the material world. Thraêtaona asks Drvâspa for power to overcome him.

l: Haoma, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Haoma is described as enlivening, healing, beautiful, lordly, and golden-eyed. Haoma sacrifices to Drvâspa on the highest height of the Haraiti Bareza and asks for Franghrasyan to be bound and brought to Husravah.

l: Franghrasyan, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Franghrasyan is identified as a Turanian murderer. Haoma asks that he be bound and brought to Husravah, and Husravah asks to kill him behind the Kaêkasta lake.

l: Husravah, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Husravah is the king who is asked to kill the bound Franghrasyan. He is also described as gallant and as having united the Arya nations into one kingdom, and he sacrifices to Drvâspa to avenge the murders of Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha.

l: Kaêkasta lake, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: The Kaêkasta lake is described as a deep lake of salt waters. Haoma asks that Franghrasyan be brought there, and Husravah offers a sacrifice behind it and asks to kill him there.

l: Airyana Vaêgah, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Airyana Vaêgah is the place where Zarathustra offers Drvâspa a sacrifice by the good river Dâitya.

l: Hutaosa, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Hutaosa is the good and noble person whom Zarathustra asks Drvâspa to bring to think, speak, and act according to the law. He also asks that she spread the Mazdean law and praise his deeds.

l: Kavi Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: Kavi Vîstâspa offers Drvâspa a sacrifice behind the waters of the river Dâitya. He asks to put several enemies and Daêva-worshippers to flight or smite them and to bring the Varedhakas and Hvyaonas to the good law.

l: libations, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: An offering of libations accompanies the sacrifices made to Drvâspa. Those who seek boons are repeatedly said to receive them while offering libations, giving gifts, sacrificing, and entreating her.

l: boon, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: The boon is the requested favor sought from Drvâspa through sacrifice and entreaty. Drvâspa grants the boons requested by Haoshyangha, Yima Khshaêta, Thraêtaona, Haoma, Husravah, Zarathustra, and Kavi Vîstâspa.

l: Law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, IX. Gôs Yast.
s: The Mazdean law is to be spread and made known by Hutaosa after Zarathustra’s request to Drvâspa. Kavi Vîstâspa also asks that the nations of the Varedhakas and Hvyaonas be brought to the good law.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: This unit concerns Ahura Mazda’s revelation to Spitama Zarathustra about Mithra, the lord of wide pastures. Mithra is presented as worthy of sacrifice and prayer, all-seeing, sleepless, protective of truthful people, and destructive toward those who lie to him. The text describes contracts, sacrifices, warfare, and Mithra’s power to grant prosperity, victory, health, and protection while bringing defeat and punishment upon his enemies.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is described as the creator of Mithra and as the source of the law of holiness. Fire is called the son of Ahura Mazda, and Ahura Mazda gives victorious strength.

l: those who lie unto Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: Men who lie unto Mithra are punished by losing strength, swiftness, eyesight, and hearing, and their weapons fail to reach their targets. Their houses and communities become desolate, and Mithra brings fear, defeat, and death upon them.

l: contract, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: The text warns that a contract must not be broken, whether it is made with an unfaithful person or with a faithful person. Mithra stands for both the faithful and the unfaithful.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: Sacrifice is repeatedly offered to Mithra with libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, speech, deeds, and rightly spoken words. Mithra is asked to accept these sacrifices and grant riches, strength, victory, good conscience, bliss, wisdom, and protection.

l: battle, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, X. Mihir Yast.
s: In battle, Mithra confronts armies, breaks their lines, spreads terror, and causes weapons to miss their marks. He supports those who honor him and brings defeat, slaughter, and flight upon hostile forces and those who lie unto him.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: This unit concerns Mithra, the lord of wide pastures, who is sleepless, ever awake, powerful, all-knowing, and undeceivable. Ahura Mazda built Mithra a dwelling on Hara Berezaiti, and Mithra watches over the material world, protects those who do not lie, and helps those who call upon him. Mithra grants riches, strength, victory, good conscience, bliss, wisdom, and other boons to the faithful, while those who lie unto Mithra lose strength, glory, and protection. The unit also describes sacrifices offered to Mithra, Haoma’s sacrifice to him, and Mithra’s destruction of enemies, Daêvas, and malice.

l: Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Mithra is the sleepless and ever-awake lord of wide pastures, powerful, all-knowing, undeceivable, and endowed with ten thousand spies. Ahura Mazda built him a dwelling on Hara Berezaiti, and Mithra watches over the material world, protects those who lie not, helps those who invoke him, grants many boons, and destroys enemies and malice.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Ahura Mazda built a dwelling for Mithra on Hara Berezaiti. He is invoked by Mithra, and his victorious strength and the glory made by him accompany Mithra.

l: Hara Berezaiti, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Hara Berezaiti is the bright mountain around which the many stars revolve. Mithra’s dwelling is there, clouds cannot reach it, and Haoma offered Mithra a sacrifice on its highest heights.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Daêvas are among the forces whose malice Mithra is asked to smite. They and the Varenya fiends flee in fear from Mithra, and Mithra protects worshippers from the fiendish hordes.

l: Haoma, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Haoma, described as enlivening, healing, fair, lordly, and golden-eyed, offered Mithra a sacrifice on Hara Berezaiti. Haoma performed the sacrifice with undefiled implements, libations, and words, and first lifted up Haomas in a heavenly mortar.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Sacrifices and libations are repeatedly offered to Mithra with his own name and proper words. Mithra is asked to accept them, gather them together with love, and lay them in the Garô-nmâna.

l: faithful, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: The faithful are the people to whom Mithra comes at the appointed time and whom he protects from harm. Mithra grants them riches, strength, victory, good conscience, bliss, wisdom, good fame, and a good soul.

l: those who lie unto Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Those who lie unto Mithra receive neither strength, vigour, glory, nor any boon from him. Mithra takes strength from their arms, swiftness from their feet, eyesight from their eyes, and hearing from their ears, and their bodies may be destroyed in battle.

l: malice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII.
s: Mithra is asked to dash in pieces the malice of malicious men and the malice of the malicious. He is also asked to smite all the malice of Daêvas, men, Yâtus, Pairikas, oppressors, the blind, and the deaf.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: This unit concerns Mithra, the lord of wide pastures, as a sleepless guardian, warrior, judge, and protector of the world. He travels across the earth in a golden chariot, armed with many weapons, and drives away Angra Mainyu, Aêshma, Bûshyãsta, and other fiends. The text teaches that Mithra observes thoughts, words, deeds, sacrifices, and lies, rewarding faithful worshippers and punishing offenders. Ahura Mazda instructs Zarathustra about proper libations and sacrifices offered to Mithra.

l: Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Mithra watches over the moving world, sees and hears all things, and travels across the earth and heavens. He drives a golden chariot with divine companions and many weapons, smites liars and enemies, drives away fiends, and grants brightness, glory, health, riches, sovereignty, and offspring to those who satisfy him. He may also bring sickness, death, poverty, sterility, and the loss of offspring to those who anger or offend him.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Ahura Mazda established Mithra to maintain and watch over the moving world. He offered a sacrifice to Mithra in the shining Garô-nmâna and instructed Zarathustra on the proper preparation and drinking of libations offered to Mithra.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda how a faithful man should drink the cleanly prepared libations offered to Mithra. He is instructed concerning bodily washing, strokes, and knowledge of the staota yêsnya.

l: the earth made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: The earth is described as wide and round, with ends lying afar. Mithra travels over its whole breadth, surveys what lies between earth and heaven, and encompasses its regions with his arms.

l: club of Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Mithra carries a club with a hundred knots and a hundred edges, made of red and strong golden brass. It is described as the strongest and most victorious of weapons, rushing forward and felling men and Daêvas.

l: chariot, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Mithra drives a beautiful, swift golden chariot from the shining Garô-nmâna. Four white, undying stallions draw it, and it bears Rashnu-Razista, Kista, Âtar, the kingly Glory, and numerous bows, arrows, spears, hammers, swords, maces, and a club.

l: libations, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Faithful worshippers give Mithra strength and energy through offered and proffered Haomas. The libations must be cleanly prepared, and those who drink them must wash and undergo prescribed strokes and know the staota yêsnya.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: The unit repeatedly calls for sacrifices to Mithra for his brightness and glory. Sacrifices may be offered with small cattle, black cattle, flying birds, Haomas, baresma, and proper words; a pious priest pleases Mithra, while an unholy priest does not.

l: Law of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: The Law of Mazda is associated with Mithra and is named among the powers and beings that an unholy priest scorns. Mithra's strength is said to be ten thousandfold when connected with the Law of Mazda.

l: Glory, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Mithra can impart brightness and glory to those who worship and satisfy him. The text repeatedly offers sacrifice for his brightness and glory and asks that brightness and glory be given to a faithful man.

l: truth, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XXIV.
s: Mithra is described as truth-speaking and as one who sees every man who tells a lie. He punishes men who lie unto him and is associated with observing evil thoughts, words, and deeds.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: This unit concerns Sraosha, the holy and fiend-smiting master of holiness, and his protection of the world and its faithful worshippers. Good prayer, the Ahuna Vairya, the word of truth, and the Law of the worshippers of Mazda are described as forces that drive away the Daêvas, Drug, and other wicked beings. Sraosha guards the creation of Mazda and the material world, fights the Mâzainya Daêvas, and protects people from fear, harm, and evil. The text offers sacrifices, prayers, libations, blessings, and glorification to Sraosha and associated holy beings.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Ahura Mazda is worshipped as supreme in holiness and foremost in doing deeds of holiness. He created Sraosha to withstand Aêshma and taught Sraosha the Law.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Zarathustra is addressed in instructions concerning good prayer, the pronouncement of protective words, and the Law. The text also worships all the words of Zarathustra and all his good deeds, done and to be done.

l: Sraosha, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Sraosha is described as holy, tall-formed, strong, fiend-smiting, and the master of holiness. He protects the poor, guards the creation of Mazda and the material world, fights the Daêvas every day and night, and protects faithful people and houses. Sacrifices, prayers, libations, and blessings are offered to him for his brightness, glory, strength, and victorious power.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: The Daêvas are driven away and made to bow or rush into darkness before Sraosha. Good prayer, the Ahuna Vairya, the word of truth, and the Law of the worshippers of Mazda are described as forces that smite or destroy them.

l: Drug, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: The Drug is turned away by good prayer and is smitten by Sraosha. Sraosha watches over the Drug and fights the fiendish Drug, which is described as most strong and world-destroying.

l: the Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: The Law of the worshippers of Mazda is called the truest giver of all good things that are offspring of the good principle. It is also named among the friends and bodies receiving sacrifice, and is described as fiend-destroying.

l: good prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Good prayer is described as taking away the friendship of fiends, turning away their senses, and driving away the Drug. It is called without deceit and without harm, and is presented as protection for people in danger or among idolaters, thieves, and Daêvas.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Sacrifice is repeatedly offered to Sraosha and to other holy beings for their brightness, glory, strength, and victorious power. The text blesses the sacrifice and prayer of Sraosha at its conclusion.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Prayer is offered with sacrifice, propitiation, and glorification to Sraosha and other holy beings. The strength and vigour of Sraosha's prayer are blessed, and prayer is associated with protection from fiends.

l: the creation of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: The creation of Mazda is guarded and maintained by Sraosha, who watches over it without sleeping. Sraosha protects it with his club uplifted from the hour when the sun is down.

l: material world, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: Sraosha protects all the material world with his club uplifted. He maintains and looks over the moving world while fighting the Mâzainya Daêvas.

l: worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XI. Srôsh Yast Hâdhôkht.
s: The worshippers of Mazda follow the Law that is called the truest giver of all good things. Their faithful people, when rich in good thoughts, good words, and good deeds, are protected by Sraosha, and their communities and houses receive sacrifice.

l: Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: This unit concerns Zarathustra questioning Ahura Mazda about the qualities and power of the Holy Word. Ahura Mazda declares that the most glorious Holy Word is true, progress-making, discerning, healthful, wise, happy, and more powerful to destroy than all other creatures. Ahura Mazda instructs that Rashnu be invoked for friendship toward the var prepared, fire, baresma, boiling milk, oil, and plant sap. Rashnu is praised as true, knowing, discerning, far-seeing, and the best doer of justice and smiter of thieves, wherever he may be.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is asked by Zarathustra about the qualities of the Holy Word and answers that its most glorious form is true, progress-making, discerning, healthful, wise, happy, and powerful to destroy. He instructs the preparation of the baresma and the invocation of his friendship toward the var prepared and associated ritual offerings. He is also invoked to come for help with the fiend-smiting Wind, the cursing thought of the wise, kingly Glory, and Saoka made by Mazda.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda to answer truthfully about what in the Holy Word is true, progress-making, discerning, healthful, wise, happy, and powerful to destroy.

l: Rashnu Razista, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: Rashnu Razista is praised and invoked as strong, tall, true, beneficent, knowing, discerning, fore-knowing, far-seeing, and the best doer of justice and smiter of thieves. His friendship is invoked toward the var prepared and its associated offerings, wherever he is located. A sacrifice, prayer, strength, and vigour are blessed for him.

l: Holy Word, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: The most glorious Holy Word is declared to be true, progress-making, fit to discern, healthful, wise, happy, and more powerful to destroy than all other creatures.

l: Law of holiness, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: Holiness is identified in the Ashem Vohû formula as the best of all good. The will of the Lord is identified in the Yathâ ahû vairyô formula as the law of holiness.

l: var prepared, Yashts (Yasts) I-XII, XII. Rashn Yast.
s: The var prepared is the object toward which Ahura Mazda and Rashnu are invoked to show friendship. It is associated with the fire, baresma, full boiling milk, oil, and sap of the plants.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda teaches Spitama Zarathustra about the power, glory, and assistance of the Fravashis of the faithful. The Fravashis sustain the sky, waters, earth, plants, animals, and unborn children, and help the faithful overcome the Daêvas and other enemies. They grant victory, health, prosperity, and protection to those who honor them through sacrifice, prayer, and devotion. During the Hamaspathmaêdha, they visit settlements seeking worship, offerings, food, and clothing, and bless those who receive them properly.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda speaks to Spitama Zarathustra about the strength, glory, help, and joy of the Fravashis of the faithful. He invokes the Fravashis for help when establishing the sky, waters, earth, and plants.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Spitama Zarathustra is instructed to proclaim the power and assistance of the Fravashis of the faithful. He is told to recite their fiend-smiting words when traveling on frightening and dangerous roads.

l: Fravashis of the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The Fravashis of the faithful sustain the sky, waters, earth, cattle, plants, and unborn children, and help preserve the material world from the Drug. They give victory, health, glory, prosperity, and protection to those who invoke and honor them, and during the Hamaspathmaêdha they visit settlements seeking sacrifice, prayer, food, and clothing.

l: Ardvi Sura Anahita, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Ardvi Sura Anahita is maintained through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis. She is described as a wide, health-giving river whose waters purify seed, wombs, and milk, and whose flow supplies the waters of the seven Karshvares.

l: Spenta-Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Spenta-Mainyu fixes and maintains the sky, waters, earth, cattle, plants, and the child conceived in the womb. The strong Fravashis sustain the sky from below after Spenta-Mainyu fixes it.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The Daêvas oppress and assault the stars and prevent them from moving, and they are among the enemies destroyed or smitten by the Fravashis. Their malice and strength are broken in battle by the Fravashis of the faithful.

l: the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The faithful receive victory, health, good glory, protection, and prosperity through the Fravashis. The Fravashis turn toward places where faithful people are devoted to holiness and are not ill-treated.

l: the material world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The material world is sustained through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis, who preserve its sky, waters, earth, plants, animals, and people. Without their help, the Drug would gain strength, dominion, and control of the material world.

l: the sky, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The sky is maintained through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis and is fixed by Ahura Mazda and Spenta-Mainyu. The Fravashis support it from below.

l: earth, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The earth is maintained through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis. It bears the bodily world, the living and the dead, mountains, streams, rivers, and plants.

l: the sea Vouru-Kasha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The sea Vouru-Kasha receives the powerful flow of Ardvi Sura Anahita. It is watched over by ninety thousand, nine thousand, nine hundred, and ninety-nine Fravashis of the faithful.

l: Waters, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The waters flow through paths made by Mazda and appointed by Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas. The Fravashis maintain the waters, show them beautiful paths, and help them nourish animals, people, and plants.

l: plants, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The plants grow through the brightness and glory of the Fravashis and along paths made by Mazda. The Fravashis show them beautiful growth and help them nourish animals, people, and the Aryan nations.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: Sacrifice, together with prayer, propitiation, and glorification, is offered to the Fravashis of the faithful. During the Hamaspathmaêdha, those who offer sacrifice with meat, clothing, and a prayer worthy of bliss receive blessings of animals, people, horses, chariots, and capable leadership.

l: the struggle against evil, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIII. Farvardîn Yast.
s: The Fravashis aid the struggle against evil by resisting the Drug, smiting the Daêvas and malicious people, breaking enemy weapons, and granting victory in battles. They support the faithful and distress those who perform evil deeds.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: The unit concerns the Fravashis of the faithful, who are worshipped as powerful beings that aid their kindred, towns, and countries. They seek and bring waters, fight for their own lands, and protect rulers who have honored them. They defend against Angra Mainyu and other dangers, while waters and plants continue to flow and grow through the action of Ahura Mazda. Ahura Mazda’s Fravashi is praised as supreme in holiness and excellence.

l: Fravashis of the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: The Fravashis of the faithful are worshipped as strong, beneficent, victorious, healing, and effective. They seek water for their kindred, boroughs, towns, and countries, fight in local battles, protect worthy rulers, and ask for praise, sacrifice, meditation, blessings, food, and clothes. They are said to have stood firm when the Good Spirit and the Evil One created the world and to have destroyed Angra Mainyu’s malice.

l: Waters, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: The waters come up from the sea Vouru-Kasha along with the Glory made by Mazda. The Fravashis seek and bring them to their kindred, boroughs, towns, and countries, and the waters of Ahura Mazda continue flowing when Angra Mainyu’s malice is destroyed.

l: the country, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: The country is sought and defended by the Fravashis of the faithful. They ask that their country have a good store and full joy, and those who win battles bring waters to it and say, 'May my country grow and increase!'.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: Angra Mainyu is named as the Evil One and as a fiend who is all death. He breaks into the creation of good holiness, but the Fravashis destroy his malice so that the waters continue flowing and the plants continue growing.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXII.
s: Ahura Mazda is described as the creator and ruler whose most beneficent waters flow forward and whose plants continue growing. His Fravashi is worshipped as the greatest, best, fairest, most solid, wisest, finest of body, and supreme in holiness.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The unit worships the good, strong, beneficent Fravashis, including those of the Amesha-Spentas, divine beings, elements, plants, animals, human figures, and holy creations. It honors Gaya Maretan as the first listener to Ahura Mazda’s thought and teaching, and Zarathustra as the first teacher and bearer of the Law. Zarathustra’s birth and growth are described as bringing joy to waters, plants, and the good creations, while the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda spreads through the seven Karshvares. The unit also praises Vîstâspa for driving back the Drug and supporting the law of Ahura and the law of Zarathustra, while describing the Daêvas as defeated and unworthy of sacrifice and prayer.

l: Fravashis of the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The Fravashis are worshipped as good, strong, beneficent, undecaying, and holy. They include those of the Amesha-Spentas, divine beings, elements, plants, animals, human figures, holy creations, and many named holy people.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are described as seven beings united in thought, speech, and deed, sharing one father and commander, Ahura Mazda. They longed for Zarathustra as lord and master of the world and praiser of Asha.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: Ahura Mazda is named as the Maker and as the father and commander of the seven Amesha-Spentas. Gaya Maretan first listened to his thought and teaching, and Zarathustra received a revelation of his Law.

l: Gaya Maretan, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: Gaya Maretan is worshipped as the first listener to the thought and teaching of Ahura Mazda. Ahura formed the race of the Aryan nations from him.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: Zarathustra is worshipped as the first thinker, speaker, and doer of what is good, and as the first Priest, Warrior, and Plougher of the ground. He first taught and possessed the Bull, Holiness, the Word, obedience to the Word, dominion, and the good things made by Mazda; his birth and growth caused the waters, plants, and good creations to rejoice.

l: Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: Vîstâspa is worshipped as a gallant, mighty-speared, lordly king who drove the Drug before him and made wide room for the holy religion. He made himself the arm and support of the law of Ahura and the law of Zarathustra.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The Daêvas are described as being driven back and brought to naught. Their creation is declared unworthy of sacrifice and prayer, and their law is opposed by the word and law of Ahura.

l: Asha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: Asha is praised as the most great, most good, and most fair. Zarathustra first pronounced its praise in the material world and is described as its praiser.

l: law of Ahura, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The law of Ahura is described as the word that destroys the Daêvas and as a revelation of the Law. Vîstâspa supports it, and Zarathustra is its first bearer among the nations.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXIII.
s: The good Law of the worshippers of Mazda is said to spread through all seven Karshvares of the earth after Zarathustra offers sacrifices with libations and bundles of baresma.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: This unit worships the Fravashis of many named holy men, women, kings, heroes, and peoples, and concludes with invocations of the Fravashis of the faithful and their ancestors. It concerns SAOSHYANT and ASTVAT-ERETA, whose future work will benefit and raise up the bodily world and withstand the Drug and evil. It praises Ahura Mazda, Sraosha, Zarathustra, the law, holiness, sacrifice, prayer, and the blessed destinies of holy men and women. It closes with blessings for houses, worshippers, the Fravashis, and the good powers associated with Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas.

l: Fravashis of the faithful, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The Fravashis of the faithful are worshipped as awful, beneficent, overpowering, and victorious. They are asked to come quickly, help, protect those in distress, bless houses, and carry hymns and worship to Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas.

l: ASTVAT-ERETA, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: ASTVAT-ERETA is the name of the future beneficent one who will make bodily creatures rise up. He will stand against the destruction of bodily creatures, the Drug of the two-footed brood, and the evil done by the faithful.

l: SAOSHYANT, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: SAOSHYANT is the name of the future Beneficent One. He will benefit the whole bodily world and stand against the destruction of bodily creatures.

l: Yima, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Yima, the son of Vîvanghant, is described as valiant and as having flocks at his wish. His Fravashi is worshipped to stand against Daêva oppression, drought that destroys pastures, and unseen death.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The Daêvas are opposed by the Fravashis and powers invoked in this unit. They include the Mâzainya Daêvas, the Daêvas associated with Aêshma, and those whose malice will be destroyed by Vîspa-taurvairi.

l: Thraêtaona, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Thraêtaona, of the Âthwya house, is invoked against itch, hot fever, humours, cold fever, incontinency, and the evil done by the Serpent.

l: law of Ahura, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The law is praised for its righteousness, innocence, and unconquerable power. It is associated with the extermination of enemies and with those who obtain holiness.

l: Keresâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Keresâspa, the Sâma and club-bearer with plaited hair, is invoked against dreadful armed forces, a destructive brigand, and a merciless man-slayer.

l: Haoshyangha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Haoshyangha is described as holy and gallant. His Fravashi is worshipped to withstand the Mâzainya Daêvas, the Varenya fiends, and the evil done by the Daêvas.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Ahura Mazda is the maker to whom the Fravashis may carry hymns and worship. The unit invokes assistance from Ahura Mazda and calls Zarathustra his follower.

l: Sraosha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Sraosha is described as holy and powerful. His assistance, together with that of Ahura Mazda and the Mãthra-Spenta, protects those in distress.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Zarathustra is described as the first and best among those heard of as worthy of sacrifice, as a follower of Ahura and performer of the law. He is also called the lord and master of the material world and the wisest, best-ruling, brightest, most glorious, and most worthy of worship among beings.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are named among those to whom the Fravashis may carry hymns and worship.

l: Yathâ ahû vairyô, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Yathâ ahû vairyô is recited with the explanation that the will of the Lord is the law of holiness.

l: Ashem Vohû, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Ashem Vohû is recited with the explanation that holiness is the best of all good.

l: holy men and women, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The holy men and women of many countries and generations are worshipped through their Fravashis, souls, spirits, consciences, and perceptions. They are described as struggling or having struggled for holiness and teaching the Law.

l: the men of the primitive law, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The men of the primitive law are worshipped as those who have been, are, or will be in houses, boroughs, towns, and countries. They are credited with obtaining houses, holiness, the Mãthra, the blessedness of the soul, and all perfections of goodness.

l: primitive law, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The primitive law is associated with the men who first listened to Ahura's teaching and struggled for holiness. Zarathustra is identified as a man of the primitive law.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Sacrifice is offered to the Fravashis and is described as making worshippers good in the eyes of Ahura Mazda. Zarathustra and the holy men and women are called worthy of sacrifice.

l: prayer, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Prayer is offered to the Fravashis and to holy beings. Zarathustra and the holy men and women are described as worthy of prayer.

l: Holiness, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: Holiness is sought, praised, and obtained by the holy men and women and by the men of the primitive law. Ashem Vohû declares that holiness is the best of all good.

l: the material world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The bodily world is the whole world that SAOSHYANT will benefit. ASTVAT-ERETA will make its bodily creatures rise up and withstand their destruction.

l: material world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XXVI.
s: The material world is the realm in which Zarathustra is called lord and master and in which he worshipped Mãthra-Spenta.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: The unit concerns Verethraghna, made by Ahura, whom Ahura Mazda identifies as the best-armed of the heavenly gods. Verethraghna appears successively as a wind, bull, horse, camel, boar, youth, raven, ram, buck, and armed man, bearing Glory, Strength, and Victory. Zarathustra learns invocations, sacrifices, protective rites, and remedies involving Verethraghna, including the use of a Vârengana feather against curses. The text promises protection and victory in battle to those who properly offer sacrifice and prayer, while condemning Daêvas, their worshippers, and improper recipients of offerings.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda identifies Verethraghna, made by Ahura, as the best-armed of the heavenly gods and answers Zarathustra's questions about him. He prescribes sacrifices, invocations, protective rites, and the proper offerings to Verethraghna.

l: Verethraghna, made by Ahura, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Verethraghna appears in ten forms, including a strong wind, bull, horse, camel, boar, youth, raven, ram, buck, and armed man. He grants virility, bodily strength, health, keen sight, victory, and protection, and he confounds or destroys hostile forces.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Zarathustra asks Ahura Mazda who is the best-armed of the heavenly gods and what remedies and invocations concern Verethraghna. He offers sacrifice and prayer to Verethraghna, seeking victorious thinking, speaking, doing, addressing, and answering.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Daêvas and their worshippers are described as enemies of the law of Mazda who spill blood, misuse offerings, and have their minds confounded and eyes made giddy. Verethraghna is invoked to destroy their malice and break their columns.

l: Aryan nations, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: The Aryan nations are told to bring libations, tie bundles of baresma, and cook a single-coloured head of cattle for Verethraghna. If the sacrifice and prayer are properly performed, hostile hordes, plagues, leprosy, venomous plants, and enemy weapons will not enter their countries.

l: Vârengana, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: A feather of the Vârengana is prescribed as a remedy for a curse or spell. Rubbing the body with it or holding a bone or feather of the bird is said to bring help, homage, glory, and protection from attack.

l: Haoma, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Haoma is offered as victorious and protective, saving one's head and protecting the body. A person who drinks it is said to win and prevail over enemies in battle.

l: Glory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Glory is borne by Verethraghna in his various forms and is described as made by Mazda, possessing health and strength. The feather of the Vârengana maintains a person's glory, and Verethraghna can confound the glory of a house with its wealth in cattle.

l: Strength, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Strength appears with Victory upon the horns or forehead of some forms of Verethraghna and is called well-shapen and made by Ahura. Strength and Victory are invoked as keepers, maintainers, forgiving and striking powers, and as signs by which victory is determined.

l: Victory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Victory accompanies Strength in Verethraghna's manifestations and is invoked in battle and martial prayer. The side that first worships Strength and Verethraghna is said to have victory stand with it.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: Sacrifice and prayer to Verethraghna include libations, baresma, Haoma, meat, sacred spells, speech, deeds, and rightly spoken words. When performed in the perfection of holiness, they bring healing, protection, strength, and victory; improper recipients cause these virtues to be withdrawn.

l: the struggle against evil, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV. Bahrâm Yast.
s: In battle, Verethraghna is invoked when armies meet to determine which side conquers and is not crushed. He is asked to smite, cut down, and destroy hostile armies, while his protection binds enemies' hands, confounds their sight, and takes hearing from their ears.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: This unit concerns Vayu, whom Ahura Mazda, Haoshyangha, Takhma Urupa, Yima, Azi Dahâka, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, Aurvasâra, Hutaosa, and unnamed maids worship through sacrifice and invocation. Vayu grants boons to several worshippers, including victory, protection, glory, prosperity, love, and husbands, but refuses Azi Dahâka’s request to empty the earth of men. Vayu describes many names and powers of himself to Zarathustra and instructs him how to worship, promising health and protection from Angra Mainyu, the Yâtus, Daêvas, and hostile men. The unit repeatedly asks for Vayu’s brightness and glory and concludes with blessings for those who worship him.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is identified as the Maker and offers sacrifice to Vayu in the Airyana Vaêgah. He asks Vayu to help him smite the creation of Angra Mainyu, and Vayu grants the boon.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Zarathustra is addressed as holy and is instructed to invoke Vayu’s names during battles, attacks, imprisonment, and other dangers. Vayu also tells Zarathustra how to use the baresma in worship.

l: Vayu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Vayu is the central deity of the unit, described as holy, powerful, swift, strong, golden-adorned, and able to affect or overcome creatures in both worlds. He grants many boons to worshippers, refuses Azi Dahâka’s request, reveals numerous names for himself, and promises health and protection to those who worship him.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is described as the Evil Spirit whose creation Ahura Mazda seeks to smite. Vayu promises that Angra Mainyu will not harm the worshipping Zarathustra.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: The Daêvas are enemies opposed by Vayu and his worshippers. Vayu grants requests to smite or overcome them, and his names are to be invoked against them.

l: Yima, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Yima sacrifices to Vayu and asks to become the most glorious of men, make animals and men undying, preserve waters and plants, and make food unfailing. Vayu grants the boon, and Yima’s reign is described as free from cold, heat, old age, death, and Daêva-made envy.

l: Azi Dahâka, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Azi Dahâka sacrifices to Vayu and asks to make all seven Karshvares empty of men. His sacrifice and request are unsuccessful, and Vayu does not grant the boon.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Sacrifice is repeatedly offered to Vayu with libations, Haoma, meat, baresma, holy spells, words, deeds, and well-spoken words. Ahura Mazda and several named figures use sacrifice to seek Vayu’s favor and request boons.

l: boon, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Boons are requested from Vayu for victory, protection, glory, prosperity, love, marriage, and other aims. Vayu grants the boons of Ahura Mazda, Haoshyangha, Takhma Urupa, Yima, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, Aurvasâra, Hutaosa, and the maids, but refuses Azi Dahâka’s boon.

l: Glory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XV. Râm Yast.
s: Brightness and glory are repeatedly offered or requested in connection with Vayu’s worship. Vayu promises health made by Mazda and full of glory, and the concluding blessing asks that the worshipper receive brightness and glory and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: This unit of the Dîn Yast concerns the most right Kista, made by Mazda and holy, and the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda. Zarathustra, Hvôvi, the Âthravans, and the king of the country are described as making sacrifices to Kista for righteousness, lawful conduct, memory, strength, peace, and other benefits. Kista is said to grant bodily strength, health, speed, hearing, and extraordinary sight. The unit ends by blessing Kista and the good Law and asking for brightness, glory, long life, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is invoked at the beginning of the unit, and the text praises the beings of whom Ahura Mazda is lord. The good Law is described as made for the worshippers of Mazda.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: Zarathustra sacrifices to the most right Kista and calls her to rise from her seat and accompany him. He seeks righteousness of thought, speech, and deed, as well as speed, strength, health, and extraordinary sight.

l: Kista, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: Kista is the most right, made by Mazda and holy, and is identified with the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda. She is praised as swift, cleansing, protective, and able to grant speed, hearing, strength, health, sturdiness, and exceptional sight.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: The good Law of the worshippers of Mazda is worshipped and receives sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, and glorification. It is described as a supplier of good stores and is blessed together with Kista at the end of the unit.

l: worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: The worshippers of Mazda are associated with the good Law and are described through their worship, sacrifices, prayers, and glorifications. The text identifies the speaker as a worshipper of Mazda and a follower of Zarathustra.

l: sacrifice, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: Sacrifice is offered to Kista and the good Law with libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, wisdom of the tongue, holy spells, words, and deeds. Zarathustra, Hvôvi, the Âthravans, and the king of the country are each said to make sacrifices for particular benefits.

l: Dîn Yast, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVI. Dîn Yast.
s: The Dîn Yast unit presents invocations, sacrifices, and praises directed toward Kista and the good Law of the worshippers of Mazda. It concludes with blessings and a request for brightness, glory, long life, and the blissful abode of the holy Ones.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: This unit concerns Ashi Vanguhi, who is worshipped as a powerful giver of glory, prosperity, health, wisdom, and victory. She grants boons to Haoshyangha, Yima Khshaêta, Thraêtaona, Haoma, Husravah, Zarathustra, and Kavi Vîstâspa. The unit also describes her family, her praise of Zarathustra, her rejection of certain libations, and her three wailings about sexual and reproductive wrongdoing. It concludes with prayers for the strength, glory, health, and blessed abode associated with Ashi Vanguhi.

l: Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Ashi Vanguhi is described as shining, powerful, healing, wise, and worthy of sacrifice. She grants boons, gives glory and prosperity, aids those who invoke her, and is identified as the daughter of Ahura Mazda and the mother’s child of Ârmaiti Spenta. She rejects libations from certain men, a courtezan, young boys, and girls who have known no man, and laments three forms of sexual or reproductive wrongdoing.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda is described as the father of Ashi Vanguhi and as the greatest and best of the gods. He tells Ashi Vanguhi not to return to the heavens or sink into the earth, but to remain and walk inside the fine kingly palace.

l: Haoma, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Haoma is honored together with the Mãthra and Zarathustra. Haoma offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi and receives the boon of binding Franghrasyan and bringing him to Husravah to be killed.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Zarathustra is described as the first mortal to recite the praise of Asha and sacrifice to Ahura Mazda and the Amesha-Spentas. Ashi Vanguhi identifies him as the one who can daunt Angra Mainyu, and she grants his request that Hutaosa follow, speak, and act according to the law and spread it.

l: Asha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Asha is praised by Zarathustra as excellent. The drinking of Haoma is said to be attended by Asha and Ashi Vanguhi.

l: Glory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Glory is associated with Ashi Vanguhi and is given by her to those whom she attends. Ashi Vanguhi is described as Glory in bodily form, and Zarathustra is told that Glory is given to his body.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu is described as evil-doing, all death, and the creator of the strongest Drug against the material world. He flees from the earth at Zarathustra’s birth and says that Zarathustra can smite and daunt him.

l: Haoshyangha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Haoshyangha offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi on the enclosure of the Hara. He asks to overcome and terrify all the Daêvas of Mâzana, and Ashi Vanguhi grants the boon.

l: Yima, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Yima Khshaêta offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi from the height Hukairya. He asks to bring fatness, flocks, and immortality to the world and remove hunger, thirst, old age, death, heat, and cold for a thousand years, and Ashi Vanguhi grants the boon.

l: Thraêtaona, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Thraêtaona offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi in the four-cornered Varena. He asks to overcome Azi Dahâka and deliver Savanghavâk and Erenavâk, and Ashi Vanguhi grants the boon.

l: Azi Dahâka, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Azi Dahâka is described as a three-mouthed, three-headed, six-eyed, thousand-sensed, powerful and fiendish Drug created by Angra Mainyu to destroy the good world. Thraêtaona asks Ashi Vanguhi for the power to overcome him.

l: Franghrasyan, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Franghrasyan is described as a Turanian murderer. Haoma receives the boon of binding and dragging him to Husravah, and Husravah receives the boon of killing him to avenge the deaths of Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha.

l: Husravah, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Husravah is described as gallant and as having united the Aryan nations into one kingdom. He offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi and asks for the power to kill Franghrasyan behind the Kaêkasta lake, receiving that boon.

l: Hutaosa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Hutaosa is described as good and noble. Zarathustra asks Ashi Vanguhi to bring her to think, speak, and act according to the law, to spread the law, and to praise his deeds.

l: Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: Kavi Vîstâspa offers a sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi behind the waters of the river Dâitya. He asks to defeat several enemies, bring the Varedhakas and Hvyaonas to the good law, and smite large numbers among the Hvyaona nations, and Ashi Vanguhi grants the boon.

l: courtezan, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: The courtezan is condemned in Ashi Vanguhi’s wailings for destroying her fruit and for bearing a child conceived by a stranger and presenting it to her husband. Ashi Vanguhi says that libations sent by the courtezan who produces untimely issues will not be accepted.

l: sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: The sacrifice to Ashi Vanguhi includes libations, Haoma and meat, baresma, wisdom of the tongue, holy spells, words or speech, deeds, and rightly-spoken words. It is offered by several figures to request glory, prosperity, victory, protection, and other boons.

l: boon granted by Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: A boon granted by Ashi Vanguhi gives the petitioner the requested power or benefit. In this unit, she grants boons to Haoshyangha, Yima Khshaêta, Thraêtaona, Haoma, Husravah, Zarathustra, and Kavi Vîstâspa.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVII. Ashi Yast.
s: The law is associated with thinking, speaking, and acting according to the law, and with the good law that Hutaosa and certain nations are asked to follow. Zarathustra asks that Hutaosa spread the law and make it known.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Âstâd Yast recounts Ahura Mazda's teaching to Spitama Zarathustra about the Aryan Glory and its powers. The Aryan Glory brings food, flocks, wealth, intelligence, money, victory, and protection against enemies and destructive fiends. Ashi Vanguhi enters the families and royal palaces of those who gladden the faithful, while Tistrya, the strong wind made by Mazda, and the Glory of the Aryas bring increase throughout the land. The unit worships holiness, the law of holiness, the healing Words, and the Glory of the Aryas.

l: Âstâd Yast, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Âstâd Yast praises Ahura Mazda, the Aryan Glory, Ashi Vanguhi, Tistrya, holiness, and the law of holiness. It records teachings, praises, worship, and blessings connected with the Glory of the Aryas.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda speaks unto Spitama Zarathustra and says that he made the Aryan Glory, Ashi Vanguhi, and the strong wind. He is praised through sacrifice, prayer, propitiation, glorification, and worship.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Zarathustra, called Spitama Zarathustra, receives Ahura Mazda's teaching about the Aryan Glory and its benefits.

l: Aryan Glory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: The Aryan Glory is made by Mazda and is rich in food, flocks, wealth, intelligence, money, and glory. It withstands Need and enemies, destroys several fiends and the non-Aryan nations, and brings increase, victory, intelligence, and virtuous offspring.

l: Ashi Vanguhi, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Ashi Vanguhi is made by Ahura Mazda and enters the family and fine royal palace of the man who gladdens the faithful with his gifts. She brings fulness of welfare, flocks, victory, intelligence, and the Glory of the Aryas.

l: Tistrya, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Tistrya is the bright, glorious star whose movement is associated with the multiplication of horses, flocks, and virtuous offspring. He is also associated with the bringing of increase and is hailed alongside the strong wind made by Mazda and the Glory of the Aryas.

l: Holiness, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: Holiness is declared to be the best of all good. It is praised and worshipped through the Ashem Vohû and through the rightly-spoken, healing, fiend-smiting Words.

l: Yathâ ahû vairyô, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XVIII. Âstâd Yast.
s: The law of holiness is identified with the will of the Lord in the Yathâ ahû vairyô. It is recited and worshipped in the unit.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The unit praises the awful kingly Glory made by Mazda and recounts its power, movements, and attachment to mountains, rulers, Zarathustra, and the Aryan nations. It names the first mountains and many other heights, including Mount Haraiti Barez and Mount Ushi-dhau Ushi-darena. It describes the future restoration of the world, when the creation becomes deathless and the Drug perishes. It also recounts how the Glory was held or pursued by Yima, Mithra, Thraêtaona, Keresâspa, Âtar, the Son of the Waters, Frangrasyan, Kavi Husravah, and Zarathustra.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Ahura Mazda made the creatures, the kingly Glory, and the Law of Mazda. He created Zarathustra and is said to oppose Frangrasyan while continually creating new creatures.

l: Zarathustra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Zarathustra is addressed by Ahura Mazda and is associated with the holy Law and the Aryan nations. The kingly Glory clave unto him, causing him to think, speak, and act according to the Law; the Ahuna Vairya he sang drove the Daêvas beneath the earth.

l: good Law of the worshippers of Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Law of Mazda is associated with holiness, righteousness, innocence, unconquerable power, and the extermination of enemies. Zarathustra thinks, speaks, and acts according to it, and the Glory of Zarathustra enters its will.

l: awful kingly Glory, made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The awful kingly Glory is made by Mazda, powerful, health-giving, victorious, and more destructive than other creatures. It passes among rulers and holy beings, escapes those who try to seize it, and helps restore the world and protect the Aryan nations.

l: the good restoration of the world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The restoration of the world occurs when the dead rise, life and immortality come, and the world becomes ever-living, increasing, and master of its wish. The Amesha-Spentas and other blessed beings are to bring it about.

l: the creation, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The creation is made prosperous by the Good Spirit and is destined to become deathless. It will no longer grow old, die, decay, or rot when the world is restored.

l: the Drug, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Drug is the opposing destructive force that rushes to kill holy beings. She and her hundredfold brood will perish when the creation becomes deathless.

l: Angra Mainyu, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Angra Mainyu created Azi Dahâka as a powerful fiendish Drug against the material world and the world of the good principle. He is named as the Evil One struggling over the Glory.

l: Good Spirit, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Good Spirit is associated with the prosperous creation and the future deathlessness of the world. He struggles with the Evil One over the Glory and flings a dart at it.

l: Daêvas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Daêvas are opposed by Zarathustra and the holy Law. They are conquered, deprived of sacrifice and prayer, driven beneath the earth by the Ahuna Vairya, and are destined to perish with the Drug.

l: Amesha-Spentas, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Amesha-Spentas are seven bright, holy, undecaying beings of one thought, speech, and deed, whose father and commander is Ahura Mazda. They govern, preserve, and will restore the creations of Ahura Mazda.

l: Aryan nations, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Aryan nations, born and unborn, are associated with the Glory that Frangrasyan tries to seize. The Glory protects them and helps preserve their lands, animals, welfare, and faithful Law.

l: seven Karshvares of the earth, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The seven Karshvares are ruled over by Haoshyangha, Takhma Urupa, Yima, and other kings who possess or receive the Glory. Frangrasyan tries to seize the Glory in order to rule over all seven.

l: Mount Haraiti Barez, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Mount Haraiti Barez is the first mountain to rise from the earth. It stretches along the shores of the land washed by waters toward the east.

l: Mount Ushi-dhau Ushi-darena, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Mount Ushi-dhau Ushi-darena is listed among the mountains that grew up after the first two mountains. It is also described as standing surrounded by waters near Lake Kãsava and the Haêtumant river.

l: Mount Ushi-darena, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Mount Ushi-darena is made by Mazda and is the seat of holy happiness. It is surrounded by waters and is connected with the place where the kingly Glory cleaves to him who grows up there.

l: the sea Vouru-Kasha, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The sea Vouru-Kasha receives the Glory after it escapes the struggle between the Good Spirit and the Evil One. The Son of the Waters seizes the Glory there, while Frangrasyan repeatedly dives into it trying unsuccessfully to seize it.

l: the Son of the Waters, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The swift-horsed Son of the Waters seizes the Glory in the sea Vouru-Kasha. He is described as a tall, shining, male god who made and shaped man and is quick to hear when worshipped.

l: Yima, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Yima rules the seven Karshvares and enjoys a reign without cold, heat, old age, death, or failing food and water. After taking delight in falsehood, he loses the Glory, which flees from him in the shape of a bird; Mithra, Thraêtaona, and Keresâspa later seize it.

l: Mithra, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Mithra seizes the Glory when it first departs from Yima. He is described as the lord of wide pastures, quick of hearing, thousand-sensed, and the most glorious of the gods in the heavens.

l: Thraêtaona, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Thraêtaona seizes the Glory the second time it departs from Yima. He is the heir of the valiant Âthwya clan and kills Azi Dahâka.

l: Azi Dahâka, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Azi Dahâka is a three-mouthed, three-headed, six-eyed, thousand-sensed fiendish Drug created by Angra Mainyu. He struggles with Âtar over the Glory, retreats when threatened, and is killed by Thraêtaona.

l: Keresâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Keresâspa seizes the Glory the third time it departs from Yima. With Manly Courage, he kills Srvara, Gandarewa, several hostile broods, and other enemies, including Snâvidhaka.

l: Manly Courage, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Manly Courage claves unto Keresâspa and is described as firm of foot, unsleeping, quick to rise, and fully awake. It accompanies him in his acts of killing hostile beings.

l: Âtar, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Âtar, the son of Ahura Mazda, tries to seize the Glory during the struggle between the Good Spirit and the Evil One. He withdraws when Azi Dahâka threatens him, then threatens Azi from behind and makes Azi retreat.

l: Frangrasyan, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Frangrasyan is a crafty Turanian ruffian who repeatedly strips himself and dives into the sea Vouru-Kasha to seize the Glory belonging to the Aryan nations and Zarathustra. He fails each time, threatens to defile corn and liquors, and is later defeated and bound by Kavi Husravah.

l: Husravah, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Kavi Husravah receives the kingly Glory and is granted strength, victory, health, offspring, long life, and dominion. He prevails over his enemies and binds Frangrasyan and Keresavazda to avenge the deaths of Syâvarshâna and Aghraêratha.

l: Ahuna Vairya, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Ahuna Vairya is sung and repeated four times by Zarathustra with increasing force. Its Glory drives all the Daêvas beneath the earth and removes sacrifice and prayer from them.

l: Victory, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: Victory cleaves to those who possess the Glory, day after day. With Victory, they conquer the havocking hordes and all who hate them; it is also associated with Kavi Husravah.

l: the Good Principle, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIX. Zamyâd Yast.
s: The Good Principle is the world and order defended by the Good Spirit, Âtar, Keresâspa, and others. Azi Dahâka and other fiends seek to destroy it, while the Glory, Victory, and the Law protect it.

l: Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The unit concerns the awful kingly Glory made by Mazda, its connection with king Vîstâspa, and its future connection with Saoshyant and Astvat-ereta. Vîstâspa follows the Law, advances the holy religion, and defeats enemies and wicked Hvyaonas. Saoshyant will restore the world, causing death, decay, hunger, thirst, the Drug, and Angra Mainyu to perish. Astvat-ereta will rise from Lake Kãsava, deliver living creatures to immortality, and lead friends who follow the good law.

l: awful kingly Glory, made by Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The awful kingly Glory made by Mazda is associated with king Vîstâspa, Saoshyant, and Astvat-ereta. It is offered sacrifice for its brightness and glory, and it cannot be forcibly seized.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Mazda is named as the maker of the awful kingly Glory, the strength and vigour of Mount Ushi-darena, and the Glory that cannot be forcibly seized.

l: Ahura Mazda, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Ahura Mazda is named in connection with the law upheld by Vîstâspa and with Astvat-ereta, who will be his friend.

l: Vîstâspa, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: King Vîstâspa thinks, speaks, and acts according to the Law and professes that Law. He drives the Drug before him, expands the holy religion, supports the law of Ahura and Zarathustra, and conquers its enemies.

l: holy religion, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The holy religion is given wide room by king Vîstâspa, who drives the Drug before him and supports the law of Ahura and Zarathustra.

l: law of Ahura, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The Law is followed in thought, speech, and action by king Vîstâspa, who professes it and uses it to destroy his foes and cause the Daêvas to retire.

l: the Drug, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The Drug is driven before king Vîstâspa as he expands the holy religion. In the future, she and her hundredfold brood will perish as it is the will of the Lord.

l: living world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The world will be restored at the wish of Saoshyant and will thereafter never grow old, die, decay, or rot. Astvat-ereta will look upon the whole living world, and his look will deliver its living creatures to immortality.

l: SAOSHYANT, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Saoshyant and his helpers will restore the world. Under his restoration, the world will become ever living and increasing, the dead will rise, and life and immortality will come.

l: the good restoration of the world, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The restoration of the world occurs when Saoshyant and his helpers restore it at its wish. It makes the world deathless, free from decay and death, and accompanied by the rising of the dead.

l: immortality, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Immortality comes when the world is restored and the dead rise. Astvat-ereta's look will also deliver the whole of the living creatures to immortality.

l: the creation, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: The creation will become deathless as the prosperous creation of the Good Spirit. The Drug and her hundredfold brood will perish even if she rushes on every side to kill the holy beings.

l: ASTVAT-ERETA, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Astvat-ereta will rise up from Lake Kãsava as a friend of Ahura Mazda and a son of Vîspa-taurvairi, knowing the victorious knowledge. He will look upon the living world with the eye of plenty, deliver its creatures to immortality, and be joined by friends who follow the good law.

l: Lake Kãsava, Yashts (Yasts) XIII-XXIV, XIV.
s: Lake Kãsava is the place from which Astvat-ereta will rise.
